clue.text: Traveller, regularly on vacation, touring country

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been emptied out, leaving only its two outside letters
touring means going all round something, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the word regularly with its insides vacated
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A traveller who regularly goes on holiday touring a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an instruction to take alternate letters, but here it is the word being emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany people are traditionally a nomadic group, so in British usage a Romany is often called a traveller.

clue.text: Insert text again, in entirety perhaps

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: found spanning the end of entirety and the start of perhaps

explanation.surface: Typing out the whole text again, perhaps in its entirety.
explanation.definitionFit: To key in text a second time is to type it once more, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Modern household item, clanger primarily in war movie that's shot

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word before it
something shot is wrecked or ruined, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of clanger
taken as written

explanation.surface: A war film featuring an anachronistic modern gadget, a clanger in the shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' seems to describe filming the movie, but it is the signal to rearrange; a clanger is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A microwave oven is a fairly recent kitchen appliance found in most homes today.

clue.text: Capital from Italy mostly weary Scotsman raised

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped
in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
to weary someone is to bore them
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A capital city where a tired Scotsman from Italy grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: BORE loses its final E to give BOR, then I + BOR + IAN is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Kenyan seat of government is one of many national capitals around the world.

clue.text: Figure they use regularly to feed anger

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the phrase before it
feeding something puts it inside, so these letters go into the next word

blocks.note: pique is irritation or resentment
the second, fourth and sixth letters of they use

explanation.surface: A figure people habitually use to stoke their anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's figure is their bodily shape and build, which is what physique describes.

clue.text: Carol maybe that man picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so we go by sound

blocks.note: him refers to that man

explanation.surface: Carol, perhaps, being the woman that man collected.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a woman's name, but it is a Christmas song.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol is a festive religious song, one example of a hymn, as the question mark signals.

clue.text: Doubting Thomas is infected, visited by Charlie

indicators.note: a place visited by someone has that visitor inside it, so one letter goes within

blocks.note: a septic wound is infected
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A doubter falls ill after a visit from a man called Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas would not believe in the resurrection without proof, so a doubting Thomas is a habitual doubter.

clue.text: Ready to replace Conservative with right peculiarity

indicators.note: to replace one thing with another swaps a letter out for a new one

blocks.note: quick as in ready or prompt with an answer
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A politician ready to swap the Tories for the right, an odd move.
explanation.walkthrough: The C in QUICK is swapped for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A quirk is an odd habit or trait, which is just what a peculiarity is.

clue.text: Apology for a dance?

blocks.note: first meaning: the polite phrase said when saying sorry
second meaning: a dance in which people may cut in and take another's partner

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like someone asking pardon for a dance; an excuse-me is also a ballroom dance where partners can be claimed by others.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock way of saying sorry, and the hyphenated noun names a partner-changing ballroom dance.

clue.text: Before start of play, tense captain's opening ploy

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a play starts with Act I
first letter of captain

explanation.surface: Before kick-off, a nervous captain opens with a ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of play' tempts you to take a P, but it means the first act of a stage play; T goes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre to gain an advantage, which is what a ploy is.

clue.text: One failing to remember a cinema's being renovated

indicators.note: a building being renovated is rebuilt, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone who forgot a cinema was shut for refurbishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is a person suffering memory loss, so someone who cannot recall things.

clue.text: Etiquette for old army officer over time

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
T is the abbreviation for time
O is the abbreviation for old
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: Proper conduct expected of a retired military officer over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word, but it supplies PRO; 'over time' places old colonel after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the formal code of correct behaviour, especially in official or diplomatic settings.

clue.text: Old ladies wanting month's rest

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter that follows is missing

blocks.note: old lady is slang for mother
M is the abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: Elderly women who need a month of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' looks like a verb about relaxing, but it means the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest means the remaining people or things, the others left over.

clue.text: Interest son in horse race

blocks.note: a stake is a share or interest in something
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father's financial interest in his son riding in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it simply joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes is the name of a horse race in which owners put up the prize money, such as the Diamond Stakes.

clue.text: Course with tenth green repeatedly out of bounds

indicators.note: out of bounds twice means both words lose their boundary letters

blocks.note: tenth without its first and last letters
green without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A golf course with the ball hit off the tenth green again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing picture hides the meal: course means a part of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is one course of a meal, the main dish in American usage or the one before it in Britain.

clue.text: Cosmetic appearing in fewer and fewer shops?

definitions.text: Cosmetic appearing in fewer and fewer shops?

blocks.clueFragment: Cosmetic appearing in fewer and fewer shops?
blocks.note: surface reading: a beauty product whose stock is dwindling across the high street
setter's reading: the product is disappearing, which names a type of face cream

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes a product becoming scarce; a cream that is disappearing from shops is literally vanishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing cream is a light moisturiser that seems to disappear into the skin, used as a make-up base.

clue.text: Creating a peer of knight nine blog furiously about

indicators.note: moving about furiously suggests wild disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight angrily blogs about being made a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility, which is how a peer is made.

clue.text: Further man upset over verse in Slovenian formerly?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: also means in addition, further
a guy is a man
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: Another man getting upset about a poem written in Slovenian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a down-clue position word: the reversed part sits above V.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia was part of Yugoslavia until 1991, so a Slovenian was once a Yugoslav, as the question mark admits.

clue.text: Fiddle Peter is running that's lacking in initiative

indicators.note: to fiddle with something is to tinker and rearrange it

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter is running a scam, which shows little drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a verb meaning to cheat, or a violin, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a bold venture, so someone without enterprise shows no drive or initiative.

clue.text: Keith awkwardly eats skinned eels and similar things

indicators.note: something done awkwardly is clumsy and out of order
skinned means the outside layer is removed, leaving just the inner letters
whatever eats takes something inside itself

blocks.note: taken as written
eels with first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Keith clumsily eating skinned eels and similar dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'and the like' means and other things of a similar kind.

clue.text: Broadcast witnesses your arrest

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken on air, so we go by sound

blocks.note: witnesses means sees, followed by your

explanation.surface: A news bulletin reports that witnesses saw you being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A seizure is the act of taking hold of someone or something by force, as in an arrest.

clue.text: Very bad cut on end of toe

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: to sever is to cut
last letter of toe

explanation.surface: A nasty cut on the end of someone's toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe describes something serious or intense, such as a very bad injury.

clue.text: Schoolboys terrified to swallow shellfish

indicators.note: to swallow is to hold something inside, so the answer lies within the words

blocks.note: found across the end of Schoolboys and start of terrified

explanation.surface: Pupils are scared of having to eat shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a bivalve mollusc, a common kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Number of Poles surrounding First Lady

indicators.note: surrounding means placed around, so the two letters go on either side

blocks.note: S and N are the south and north poles
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A number of Polish people gathered around the president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, but it means Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a whole number, one more than six.

clue.text: Back island runner to lose lead for sure

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the whole wordplay is read from right to left
losing the lead means losing the first letter of the word before

blocks.note: Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was exiled
a miler is an athlete who runs the mile

explanation.surface: Backing an island athlete who is sure to lose the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: MILER drops its M to give ILER; ELBA + ILER is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reliable can be depended on, so it is sure or certain.

clue.text: Barely deserved

blocks.note: first meaning: only ..., by a narrow margin
second meaning: fair, as in a merited punishment

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb for scarcely managing and as an adjective for something fair or merited.

clue.text: I have to stop drunken revel

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, sitting inside the gap

blocks.note: lit up is slang for drunk
I've is the short form of I have

explanation.surface: Someone declares they must give up drunken partying.
explanation.definitionFit: To live it up is an idiom for enjoying oneself lavishly, which is to revel.

clue.text: Useless female subsequently useful?

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
utile is a rare word for useful

explanation.surface: A woman who was useless turns out to be useful later?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contradicts itself, useless then useful, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile describes an effort that achieves nothing, so it is pointless or without value.

clue.text: Lengthy quarrel at event sadly involving daughter

indicators.note: sadly means badly or wrongly, so the letters come out in a new order
involving means taking in, so one letter goes inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A long-running family row that sadly involved a daughter at some occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud, often between families, which is a long-running quarrel.

clue.text: Old measure of class

blocks.note: first meaning: an old unit of distance, roughly three miles
second meaning: a level of quality, as in out of someone's class

explanation.definitionFit: It was a historic unit of length of about three miles, and also a grade of ability, as in a different league.
